message.forecast-snapshot-exists: Today’s snapshot already exists; outcomes were updated.
label.roi-what-if: What if you spent more on ads?
message.forecast-how-1: Each of the {n} users gets a chance of buying. It starts from the conversion rate of past trial users who behaved like them in their first 3 trial days (active days and whether they activated; see “What predicts conversion”), pulled toward the overall {rate} so small groups don’t swing to extremes.
message.forecast-how-2: That chance is spread over time by when people usually buy: a few during the trial, most in the days right after it ends, and a tail up to {days} days later. Someone 10 days past their trial end has used up most of their buying window, so their chance for the next 7 days is small.
message.forecast-how-3: The headline adds up everyone’s chances: 20 users at 10% each make 2 expected customers. {x} in the next 7 days is that sum; it can be a fraction because it is an average.
message.forecast-how-4: The range comes from simulating {runs} possible outcomes (each user buys or not, with their chance) and taking the middle 80%.
message.forecast-p-tip: Chance this user buys in the next 14 days. Tap or hover a value for the 7-day chance, the chance of buying at all, and the user’s behavior group.
message.forecast-range-tip: The middle 80% of {runs} simulated outcomes. Few users with low chances make this range wide.
message.forecast-risk-tip: Trial ended, not bought: access stopped and they haven’t paid yet. Low engagement: at most 1 active day in the first 3 trial days. Not activated: never reached activation_complete.
message.roi-proj-beyond: This is more than 3× anything you've spent before, so treat it as a rough guess.
message.roi-proj-thin: Only {n, plural, one {# of these months} other {# of these months}} had ad spend, so these numbers will move as more months come in.
message.forecast-scope-short: Current trials · not filtered by signup window
message.forecast-p-detail: Next 7 days: {p7} · next 14 days: {p14} · buys at all: {total}. Behavior group: {segment}.
message.roi-proj-simple: At {spend} a month in ads, about {visitors} people would visit the website each month. In the past, 1 in {n} visitors became a paying customer, so that would be about {customers} new paying customers a month.
message.roi-payback-none: Doesn't pay for itself within 12 months
message.roi-outlook-how: How this works: ad dollars buy website visits at what a click cost before ({months}: Meta {meta}, Google {google}). Every visit, from ads or not, becomes a paying customer at your past rate. Today's money in, from all your current customers, stays flat. Extra customers keep paying: {yearly}% choose yearly and pay {yearlyPrice} up front; the rest pay {monthly} a month, and like your past monthly customers {m6}% are still paying after 6 months and {m12}% after 12. Yearly renewals fall after month 12 ({renewal}% of {renewalN} past yearly customers renewed).
label.roi-break-even-title: Break-even: when do ads pay for themselves?
label.roi-be-chart-title: Net income per $100 of ads within 12 months (blended)
message.roi-be-headline: Your ads pay for themselves within {window} if at least {need} of ad visitors become paying customers. You're at {have} ({source}).
message.roi-be-no-spend: No paid website visits with ad spend in these months, so there is no break-even to show yet.
message.roi-be-measured-how: Measured: {payers, plural, one {# paying customer} other {# paying customers}} traced back to a paid click (the UTMs their signup recorded, then their first payment on the web or in the app stores), out of {visits} paid visits at least {days} days old, long enough for the trial and first billing to play out. It replaces the estimate once {min} paying customers are traced. App signups from iOS never carry UTMs, so this undercounts until more customers sign up on the web or on Android.
message.roi-be-estimate-how: Estimated: paid visits × (web signups + store taps × tap-to-signup) ÷ visits × trial-to-paying.
message.roi-be-estimate-web: {rate} of paid visits signed up on the web (observed).
message.roi-be-estimate-taps: {rate} of paid visits tapped an App Store or Google Play badge (observed), and {tapToSignup} of taps are taken to end in an app signup ({assumed, select, yes {assumed default; all traffic's app signups ÷ taps is {ceiling}, but that counts installs from store search too} other {your setting}}).
message.roi-be-estimate-paying: {rate} of trials became paying customers over the last {months} completed months (observed, all trials; a shorter window swings because recent trials have not all had the chance to pay).
message.roi-be-chart-note: Each paying customer is worth about {value} within 12 months. Left of the break-even line, $100 of ads brings in less than $100 within a year.
message.roi-be-move-cost: Cutting {channel} cost per visit to {cost} lowers its break-even rate to {rate} (now {now}).
message.roi-be-move-yearly: Raising the yearly plan share from {from}% to {to}% lowers the blended break-even to {rate} (now {now}).
message.roi-other-costs-tip: Hosting, email and other costs per paying customer per month. Subtracted from what a customer is worth, so they raise the break-even rate.
message.roi-fixed-costs-tip: Costs you pay every month regardless of customers. They don't change the break-even rate per visit; they're taken off net income in the "What if" outlook.
message.roi-tap-to-signup-tip: Share of store-badge taps that end in an app signup. Leave empty for the default (20%: about 30% of store page visits install, about 65% of installs sign up). All traffic's app signups ÷ taps is {ceiling}, but that includes people who found the app in store search.
message.roi-be-few-months: Only {n, plural, one {# month has} other {# months have}} had meaningful ad spend so far, so these rates will move as more months come in.
message.roi-be-value-how: A new paying customer brings in about {v1} in the first month and {v12} within 12 months: {yearly}% choose yearly ({yearlyNet} after fees, up front), the rest pay {monthlyNet} a month while they stay ({m6}% still paying after 6 months, {m12}% after 12, from {n} past monthly customers). Yearly renewals ({renewal}%) only come in month 13, so they are not counted.
message.roi-be-ad-retention: Ad-acquired customers ({n} with 3+ months of history) keep paying like this: {m6}% after 6 months, {m12}% after 12.
message.roi-be-ad-retention-pending: The retention curve is from all past customers, not ad-acquired ones: {n} customers are traced to ads so far, {three} with 3+ months of history; their own curve shows once {min} have.
message.roi-be-costs-included: Break-even includes other costs of {amount} per paying customer a month.
message.roi-be-costs-excluded: Break-even does not include other costs (none set).
message.roi-be-paid-visits-how: Paid visits are the first page of a session on the marketing site from a Google ad (gclid, or tagged google / cpc) or a Meta ad (tagged utm_medium=paid from Facebook, Instagram, Audience Network, Threads or Messenger), leaving out bots and logged-in app sessions. Cost per visit is that channel's website-campaign spend over its paid visits; app-install campaigns are left out because their clicks go straight to the stores.
message.roi-proj-paid: At {spend} a month in ads, about {paid} of the {visitors} monthly website visitors would come from ads. Ad visitors become paying customers at about 1 in {meta} (Meta) and 1 in {google} (Google), {source}, rather than the 1 in {all} of all visitors, so that would be about {customers} new paying customers a month.
message.roi-per-100: Each extra $100 on Meta returns about {meta} within 12 months; on Google about {google}.
message.roi-proj-costs: Includes other costs of {perCustomer} per paying customer a month and {fixed} of fixed costs a month.
message.roi-outlook-how-paid: How this works: ad dollars buy paid website visits at what a paid visit cost in {months} (Meta {meta}, Google {google}), and those visits become paying customers at their channel's rate from the break-even panel. Today's money in, from all your current customers, stays flat. Extra customers keep paying: {yearly}% choose yearly and pay {yearlyPrice} up front; the rest pay {monthly} a month, and like your past monthly customers {m6}% are still paying after 6 months and {m12}% after 12. Yearly renewals fall after month 12 ({renewal}% of {renewalN} past yearly customers renewed).
message.roi-be-rolling-note: Paid visits, ad spend, store taps and signups cover the last 30 days, so this month counts too. Customer value, trial-to-paying and the "What if" baseline (money in, other visitors) only exist per month, so they come from completed months.
label.roi-extra-over-year: Extra money over the next 12 months
message.roi-payoff-answer: Every $100 on ads brings back about {amount} within a year.
message.roi-payoff-no-data: Not enough ad traffic in this period to tell yet.
message.roi-payoff-break-even: To break even, about 1 in {need} ad visitors needs to become a paying customer. Right now it's about 1 in {have}.
message.roi-payoff-how-visits: Ad money buys website visits at what a visit from each ad cost in {period}: Meta {meta}, Google {google}.
message.roi-payoff-how-convert: About 1 in {meta} Meta visitors and 1 in {google} Google visitors become paying customers. That comes from what ad visitors did: signed up on the website, or tapped an App Store or Google Play button (assuming 1 in {taps} of those sign up in the app), times the share of trials that end up paying ({paying}%).
message.roi-payoff-how-value: A paying customer brings in about {value} in their first year, after fees: {yearly}% pay for a year up front, the rest pay monthly while they stay ({m12}% are still paying after 12 months).
message.roi-payoff-how-today: The sliders only change new customers from ads; everyone already paying stays as is. Only {n, plural, one {# month has} other {# months have}} had real ad spend so far, so expect these numbers to move.
